newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso falls on central bank dlr buying.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso falls on central bank dlr buying.

text.p: *Central Bank dollar purchases seen at $60 million
The Philippine peso fell to 26.271 to the dollar at the close on Thursday from 26.265 as banks took their cue from the Central Bank.
Late trades saw the Central Bank buying dollars at 26.260 to 26.266 pesos, dealers said.
"The Central Bank was aggressive in buying," a local bank trader said. Dealers estimate the Central Bank purchased as much as $60 million.
One dealer said the Central Bank was recovering the dollars it sold on Tuesday, while another said it was buying to meet some loan payments this month.
The peso nudged to a day-low of 26.277 pesos after a strong opening. At the start, "the sentiment was for a strong peso since there was not much demand for dollars," another dealer said.
The day's average showed a stronger peso at 26.265 versus 26.267 on Wednesday, with turnover swelling to $177.50 million from $139.90 million.
The Central Bank will dictate the trend on Friday, traders said. - LILIAN KARUNUNGAN (632) 841-8937
